title: INDUSTRIALS SCORECARD: POWELL EPS +59%, STERLING -31% AFTER RECORD RESULTS, AECOM +6.9%
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Industrials and energy names put up a mixed scorecard today: some  
clean beats, some ugly misses, a guidance withdrawal, and Sterling  
falling about 31% in 30 days despite record Q3 results while an  
average target still implies about 110% upside. One tanker target uses  
only the bullish subset of estimates, which is flagged below.  
  
Here is the scorecard from today's write-ups.  
  
\*\*1. Powell Industries (POWL)\*\* — Fiscal Q4 revenue was $396.7  
million, up 33% from $298.0 million a year earlier. Diluted EPS was  
$2.23, up 59% from $1.41 and well above estimates, with a record  
backlog.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/powell-industries-powl-delivers-strong-fiscal-q4-results-with-record-backlog-39325/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/powell-industries-powl-delivers-strong-fiscal-q4-results-with-record-backlog-39325/)  
  
\*\*2. Powell Industries (POWL)\*\* — The $255 central target is the  
average of the three most recent verified targets ($235 Cantor  
Fitzgerald, $250 J.P. Morgan, $275 Roth MKM). From about $153, that  
implies about 67% upside. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/powell-industries-powl-evaluating-the-path-to-the-255-analyst-target-39334/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/powell-industries-powl-evaluating-the-path-to-the-255-analyst-target-39334/)  
  
\*\*3. AECOM (ACM)\*\* — Adjusted EPS of $1.63 beat the $1.59 consensus by  
$0.04, and the stock jumped 6.9%, per the write-up. Revenue of $3.9  
billion was down 7% and missed the $4.1 billion estimate, while net  
service revenue rose 3% to $1.92 billion.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/aecom-acm-jumps-6-9-on-q4-earnings-beat-and-record-backlog-39321/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/aecom-acm-jumps-6-9-on-q4-earnings-beat-and-record-backlog-39321/)  
  
\*\*4. AECOM (ACM)\*\* — The $81 central target is the average of roughly  
a dozen current analyst targets, rounded from about $80.73. From a  
last close near $72.50, reaching $81 would take about a 12% advance.  
Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/aecom-acm-analyst-consensus-points-to-modest-12-upside-39326/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/aecom-acm-analyst-consensus-points-to-modest-12-upside-39326/)  
  
\*\*5. Sterling Infrastructure (STRL)\*\* — Shares fell about 31% over 30  
days, from $424.36 on October 16 to $292.39 on November 13, per the  
write-up, not a live quote. That slide came despite record Q3 results,  
including revenue up 127% to $1.56 billion and adjusted EPS up 118% to  
$7.58.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/sterling-infrastructure-strl-drops-31-in-30-days-despite-record-results-38668/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/sterling-infrastructure-strl-drops-31-in-30-days-despite-record-results-38668/)  
  
\*\*6. Sterling Infrastructure (STRL)\*\* — The $635 central target is the  
average of seven recent firm-attributed targets. From about $300,  
reaching $635 would take a gain of about 110%. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/sterling-infrastructure-strl-analyst-targets-point-to-110-upside-potential-38671/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/sterling-infrastructure-strl-analyst-targets-point-to-110-upside-potential-38671/)  
  
\*\*7. Red Cat (RCAT)\*\* — Fiscal Q3 revenue was $11.8 million, up 22%  
from $9.6 million, but far below a consensus of about $40.7 million.  
The net loss widened to $40.4 million, or $0.26 a share, missing a  
$0.20 consensus loss, and the company withdrew guidance.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/red-cat-holdings-rcat-reports-q3-revenue-growth-but-widens-losses-and-withdraws-guidance-39354/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/red-cat-holdings-rcat-reports-q3-revenue-growth-but-widens-losses-and-withdraws-guidance-39354/)  
  
\*\*8. TOYO\*\* — Q3 revenue was $129.0 million, down 4.8% and below a  
consensus of about $141 million. Diluted EPS was $0.10, missing about  
$0.31 and down from $0.66 a year earlier.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/toyo-co-ltd-toyo-reports-q3-2026-earnings-shortfall-amid-trade-policy-shifts-39380/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/toyo-co-ltd-toyo-reports-q3-2026-earnings-shortfall-amid-trade-policy-shifts-39380/)  
  
\*\*9. Montauk Renewables (MNTK)\*\* — Q3 revenue rose 10.9% to $50.19  
million. Net income fell to $2.14 million from $5.21 million, and EPS  
was $0.01, down from $0.04.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/montauk-renewables-mntk-reports-q3-2026-revenue-growth-of-10-9-with-margin-pressure-39357/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/montauk-renewables-mntk-reports-q3-2026-revenue-growth-of-10-9-with-margin-pressure-39357/)  
  
\*\*10. Ballard Power Systems (BLDP)\*\* — Revenue fell 31% to $22.5  
million, well below a consensus of about $32.7 million. Gross margin  
rose five points to 20%, and operating expenses fell 20% to $28.0  
million.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/ballard-power-systems-bldp-delivers-mixed-q3-2026-results-during-strategic-shift-39356/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/ballard-power-systems-bldp-delivers-mixed-q3-2026-results-during-strategic-shift-39356/)  
  
\*\*11. ESAB\*\* — The $110 central target is the average of the most  
recent individual targets reviewed, spanning about $95 to $130. From a  
close of $83.25, that implies about 32% upside. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/esab-corporation-nyse-esab-can-shares-reach-the-110-target-for-32-upside-38526/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/esab-corporation-nyse-esab-can-shares-reach-the-110-target-for-32-upside-38526/)  
  
\*\*12. Aramark (ARMK)\*\* — Fiscal Q4 revenue was $5.29 billion, up about  
5% as reported and 12% organically. Adjusted EPS was $0.71, up about  
25% on a constant-currency basis but below a consensus of about $0.75,  
and the write-up says guidance came in slightly below expectations.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/aramark-armk-delivers-strong-organic-growth-in-q4-but-guidance-comes-in-slightly-below-expectations-39319/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/aramark-armk-delivers-strong-organic-growth-in-q4-but-guidance-comes-in-slightly-below-expectations-39319/)  
  
\*\*13. Aramark (ARMK)\*\* — The $68 central target is the average of 12  
verified targets, rounded from about $68.50. From a close near $55.37,  
that implies about 23% upside. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/aramark-armk-could-see-23-upside-to-68-target-on-strong-growth-39322/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/aramark-armk-could-see-23-upside-to-68-target-on-strong-growth-39322/)  
  
\*\*14. Frontline (FRO)\*\* — The $61.50 figure is the average of the two  
targets that sit above the current price (Evercore ISI $53 and BTIG  
$70), not the full four-analyst mean of about $50.50. The full range  
runs from $39.15 to $70. Target, not a promise — and that $61.50 math  
is a bullish subset.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/frontline-plc-fro-is-31-upside-to-61-50-still-in-reach-38479/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/frontline-plc-fro-is-31-upside-to-61-50-still-in-reach-38479/)  
  
\*\*15. Danaos (DAC)\*\* — Danaos is scheduled to report Q3 after the U.S.  
close on Monday, November 23, 2026. Consensus is about $7.39 a share  
in adjusted earnings on revenue of about $276.63 million, up from  
$6.75 and $260.73 million a year earlier.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/danaos-corporation-dac-q3-2026-earnings-preview-key-expectations-and-what-matters-39329/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/danaos-corporation-dac-q3-2026-earnings-preview-key-expectations-and-what-matters-39329/)  
  
Sterling is down 31% in 30 days after record results, and the average  
target still implies 110% upside. Does that look like a setup or a  
warning?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's (Nov 16) write-ups,  
using intraday or latest-close prices, not live quotes. Price targets  
are targets, not promises.
